import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Set style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
sns.set_palette("husl")

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create figure with subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(20, 16))

# 1. Income distribution by education level
ax1 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 1)
income_edu = df.groupby('Education')['Income'].agg(['mean', 'median', 'std']).sort_values('mean')
income_edu['mean'].plot(kind='bar', ax=ax1, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')
ax1.set_title('Average Income by Education Level', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
ax1.set_ylabel('Average Income ($)', fontsize=12)
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Spending categories comparison
ax2 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 2)
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 
                 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_means = df[spending_cols].mean()
spending_means.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax2, color='lightcoral', edgecolor='black')
ax2.set_title('Average Spending by Product Category', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Product Category', fontsize=12)
ax2.set_ylabel('Average Amount Spent ($)', fontsize=12)
ax2.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 3. Purchase channels distribution
ax3 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 3)
purchase_cols = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases', 'NumDealsPurchases']
purchase_means = df[purchase_cols].mean()
purchase_means.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax3, color='lightgreen', edgecolor='black')
ax3.set_title('Average Purchases by Channel', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Purchase Channel', fontsize=12)
ax3.set_ylabel('Average Number of Purchases', fontsize=12)
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 4. Income vs Total Spending scatter plot
ax4 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 4)
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)
scatter = ax4.scatter(df['Income'], df['TotalSpending'], 
                      c=df['NumWebVisitsMonth'], cmap='viridis', 
                      alpha=0.6, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax4.set_title('Income vs Total Spending', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Income ($)', fontsize=12)
ax4.set_ylabel('Total Spending ($)', fontsize=12)
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax4)
cbar.set_label('Web Visits per Month', fontsize=12)

# 5. Age distribution histogram
ax5 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 5)
current_year = 2024  # Assuming current year for age calculation
df['Age'] = current_year - df['Year_Birth']
ax5.hist(df['Age'], bins=30, color='gold', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax5.set_title('Customer Age Distribution', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=12)
ax5.set_ylabel('Number of Customers', fontsize=12)
ax5.axvline(df['Age'].mean(), color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
            label=f'Mean: {df["Age"].mean():.1f}')
ax5.legend()

# 6. Family composition analysis
ax6 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 6)
df['TotalChildren'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']
family_counts = df['TotalChildren'].value_counts().sort_index()
family_counts.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax6, color='orchid', edgecolor='black')
ax6.set_title('Number of Children per Household', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Number of Children', fontsize=12)
ax6.set_ylabel('Number of Households', fontsize=12)

# 7. Campaign acceptance rates
ax7 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 7)
campaign_cols = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 
                 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
campaign_acceptance = df[campaign_cols].mean() * 100
campaign_acceptance.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax7, color='lightblue', edgecolor='black')
ax7.set_title('Campaign Acceptance Rates', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax7.set_xlabel('Campaign', fontsize=12)
ax7.set_ylabel('Acceptance Rate (%)', fontsize=12)
ax7.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax7.set_ylim(0, 100)

# 8. Recency distribution
ax8 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 8)
ax8.hist(df['Recency'], bins=30, color='lightseagreen', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax8.set_title('Days Since Last Purchase', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax8.set_xlabel('Days Since Last Purchase', fontsize=12)
ax8.set_ylabel('Number of Customers', fontsize=12)
ax8.axvline(df['Recency'].mean(), color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
            label=f'Mean: {df["Recency"].mean():.1f}')
ax8.legend()

# 9. Marital status distribution
ax9 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 9)
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
marital_counts.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax9, color='salmon', edgecolor='black')
ax9.set_title('Customer Marital Status Distribution', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax9.set_xlabel('Marital Status', fontsize=12)
ax9.set_ylabel('Number of Customers', fontsize=12)
ax9.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Adjust layout and save
plt.suptitle('Customer Segmentation Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.close()
